content.value_statement: AIR designs can contain subtle unconstrained states, selector gaps, and degree errors. This skill guides structured reviews that connect each protocol claim to enforceable constraints.
actual_capabilities: Explains finite-field and polynomial concepts used in AIR systems.
Reviews trace columns, row semantics, selectors, and boundary constraints.
Identifies common soundness failures in transition, lookup, permutation, and memory arguments.
Creates a constraint map from semantic claims to enforcing equations.
Performs degree-accounting checks for quotient and composition polynomials.
Proposes adversarial witness tests for AIR review.
limitations: It provides guidance and does not execute or formally verify an AIR implementation.
It cannot replace an independent cryptographic audit of production proving systems.
Its conclusions depend on the complete constraints and protocol details you provide.
It does not implement proving, verification, or polynomial commitment code.

use_cases.title: Audit a new AIR design
use_cases.description: Map each execution rule to constraints and identify unconstrained columns or selector gaps before implementation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a security review
use_cases.description: Build an adversarial test plan for boundary conditions, memory consistency, and challenge binding.

use_cases.title: Learn AIR soundness methods
use_cases.description: Study practical checks for trace design, degree limits, and common STARK vulnerability patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Explain an AIR concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain why every AIR trace column needs constraints. Use a small conceptual example without implementation code.

prompt_templates.title: Check selector design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this selector design: [describe selectors and gated constraints]. Check Booleanity, coverage, exclusivity, and ghost modes.

prompt_templates.title: Build a constraint map
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a constraint map for this AIR: [describe columns, row meanings, and rules]. List each claim, its enforcing constraint, and gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Conduct an adversarial AIR review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this AIR specification for soundness: [provide full specification]. Test transitions, boundaries, lookups, memory, quotient degree, and Fiat-Shamir binding. Rank findings and suggest fixes.

output_examples.input: Review a selector that activates arithmetic constraints only when an opcode flag is set.
output: Check that the opcode flag is Boolean.
Check that every row has an active selector or an explicit padding rule.
Verify that constraints prevent all selectors from being zero.

output_examples.input: Assess a memory consistency argument with address, timestamp, value, and write flag columns.
output: Confirm that timestamps are constrained to increase for each address.
Verify that reads bind to the latest preceding write.
Ensure a permutation argument links the sorted memory log to CPU events.

best_practices: Provide complete column definitions, constraints, domains, and transcript order before requesting a review.
Test every claimed rule with a counterexample trace that attempts to bypass it.
Track constraint degrees after selectors and boundary factors are applied.
anti_patterns: Do not treat documented column meanings as constraints.
Do not assume selector coverage without enforcing it algebraically.
Do not reuse Fiat-Shamir challenges across independent arguments.

faq.question: What is an AIR?
faq.answer: An Algebraic Intermediate Representation describes computation as polynomial constraints over a finite field.

faq.question: Can this skill find unconstrained columns?
faq.answer: It can guide a review that compares each column definition with the constraints you provide.

faq.question: Does it implement STARK proofs?
faq.answer: No. It provides design and review guidance, not a proving or verification implementation.

faq.question: What information should I provide for an audit?
faq.answer: Provide trace columns, row semantics, all constraints, evaluation domains, public inputs, and transcript ordering.

faq.question: Can it review lookup and permutation arguments?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers boundary checks, challenge binding, duplicate handling, and compression soundness.

faq.question: Does a positive review guarantee security?
faq.answer: No. Production systems require complete specifications, testing, and independent expert cryptographic review.
